text: Although the importance of mechanical tension in promoting muscle growth is indisputable, there is evidence that other factors also play a role in the hypertrophic process. One such factor proposed to be of particular relevance to exercise-induced anabolism is metabolic stress (230, 244, 255). Simply stated, metabolic stress is an exercise-induced accumulation of metabolites, particularly lactate, inorganic phosphate, and H+ (261, 272). However, it should be noted that approximately 4,000 metabolites have been detected in human serum (294), and thus other metabolic byproducts may be relevant to training-related adaptations as well.
